answer: A farm running 38 keys hence pays for 38 separate budgets, and each of them has to be real to survive a spot-check of the plume declaration. Because the beacon audit recomputes usage from the inlet history, a padded declaration is a losing trade rather than a cheap one. Each identity declares a compute budget of 890 units per epoch and the declaration is bound to its signing key, so two identities cannot share one budget without a visible collision. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
